details: Classifying what a user wants from an utterance — e.g. book_flight or check_balance — in task-oriented dialogue systems. Accurate intents drive routing in assistants, IVR systems, and support bots.

explainer.lead: Intent detection classifies what a user wants from an utterance, such as book_flight or check_balance. It matters because accurate intents drive routing in assistants, IVR systems and support bots.

tiers.eli5: It is how a system figures out which task you are asking for, like a receptionist sending you to the right desk.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build it as a classifier over utterances in task-oriented dialogue systems and route on its output; a pitfall is that misclassified intents send users down the wrong path.
tiers.paperLevel: Framed as classifying a user's want from an utterance into labels such as book_flight or check_balance within task-oriented dialogue systems; accurate intents drive routing.

explainer.example: A user says they want a flight to Paris, the system classifies the utterance as book_flight, and the booking flow starts.
